feature: Go deny entries match exactly one package
description: For Go imports, a deny entry denies only the import path equal to it. The scaffolded Go deny list names each I/O package it used to reach by prefix, so pure packages like net/netip and net/url are allowed.

specs.description: A Go deny entry denies the package it names
specs.when: judge is called for the Go import "net"
specs.then: The verdict is denied

specs.description: A Go deny entry does not deny a pure package whose path starts with it
specs.when: judge is called for the standard-library Go import "net/netip"
specs.then: The verdict is not denied, and the import is let through as standard library

specs.description: Go net/url is not denied by a deny entry of net
specs.when: judge is called for the standard-library Go import "net/url"
specs.then: The verdict is not denied

specs.description: A Go deny entry does not reach a package below it on a / boundary, even an I/O one
specs.when: judge is called for the Go import "net/http"
specs.then: The verdict is not denied by the "net" entry, because it names only net

specs.description: A Go deny entry of os does not deny os/user or os/signal
specs.when: judge is called for the Go imports "os/user" and "os/signal"
specs.then: Neither verdict is denied

specs.description: A deny entry naming a deeper path does not deny its parent
specs.when: judge is called for the Go import "net"
specs.then: The verdict is not denied

specs.description: A Go deny entry does not match a path that only shares its leading characters
specs.when: judge is called for a Go import "network"
specs.then: The verdict is not denied by the "net" entry

specs.description: Rust deny entries still match below the path
specs.when: judge is called for the Rust import "std::fs::File"
specs.then: The verdict is denied, as before

specs.description: Rust std::net still covers std::net::IpAddr
specs.when: judge is called for the Rust import "std::net::IpAddr"
specs.then: The verdict is denied

specs.description: TypeScript deny entries still match below the path
specs.when: judge is called for the TypeScript import "node:fs/promises"
specs.then: The verdict is denied, as before

specs.description: Python deny entries match as they did before this ADR
specs.given: Language Python, a deny entry and an import below it that the previous rule denied
specs.when: judge is called for that Python import
specs.then: The verdict is the same as under the previous rule

specs.description: Go allow entries still match below the path
specs.given: Language Go, allow = ["example.com/lib"], deny empty, and a non-standard-library import "example.com/lib/sub"
specs.when: judge is called for "example.com/lib/sub"
specs.then: The verdict is allowed, as before

specs.description: An exact Go deny match still beats an allow
specs.when: judge is called for the Go import "net"
specs.then: The verdict is denied

specs.description: A Go standard-library deny entry denies exactly the path equal to it; a module deny entry covers the packages below it
specs.given: Any Go deny list D, an empty allow list, and any Go import path p
specs.when: judge is called for p
specs.then: The deny rule denies p if and only if p equals some entry of D, or some entry of D whose first path element has a dot is a prefix of p on a / boundary. No standard-library entry denies a path that merely starts with it.

specs.description: Non-Go deny entries and all allow entries keep their behaviour
specs.given: Any non-Go language (Rust, TypeScript, Python) with any import, allow and deny, or any Go import judged only against allow entries
specs.when: judge is called
specs.then: The verdict equals the verdict under the previous below-the-path matching

specs.description: The scaffolded Go deny names each I/O package explicitly
specs.when: Its Go deny entries are read
specs.then: They are os, os/exec, os/signal, os/user, net, net/http, net/http/httptest, net/http/httputil, net/http/pprof, net/rpc, net/rpc/jsonrpc, net/smtp, database/sql, io/ioutil, plugin and http

specs.description: A scaffolded domain is still denied I/O packages once reached by prefix
specs.given: A project scaffolded from the template, judging a Go domain import
specs.when: judge is called for "net/smtp", "os/user", "net/http/pprof" and "net/rpc/jsonrpc"
specs.then: Each verdict is denied

specs.description: A scaffolded domain may use pure network-name packages
specs.given: A project scaffolded from the template, judging a Go domain import
specs.when: judge is called for "net/netip", "net/url", "net/mail" and "net/textproto"
specs.then: None is denied. Each is let through as standard library.

specs.description: The scaffolded Go deny does not list the pure packages
specs.when: Its Go deny entries are read
specs.then: They contain none of net/netip, net/url, net/mail or net/textproto

specs.description: The template keeps the bare http entry
specs.when: Its deny entries are read
specs.then: "http" is still present and has not been dropped

specs.description: The new template denies every Go I/O package the old template denied by prefix
specs.given: Each of os, net, http, net/http, database/sql, os/exec, io/ioutil, plugin, os/signal, os/user, net/http/httptest, net/http/httputil, net/http/pprof, net/rpc, net/rpc/jsonrpc and net/smtp
specs.when: judge is called for that Go import under the scaffolded rules
specs.then: The verdict is denied

specs.description: A Go module deny entry still covers the packages below it
specs.when: A Go domain file imports github.com/jackc/pgx/v5/pgxpool
specs.then: The verdict is denied

specs.description: A Go module deny entry does not match a path that only shares its leading characters
specs.when: A Go domain file imports github.com/jackc/pgx/v5x/pool
specs.then: The verdict is not denied by that entry
